newsitem.title: USA: Atrix says Atridox trials successful.
newsitem.headline: Atrix says Atridox trials successful.

text.p: Atrix Laboratories Inc said Friday that its Phase III clinical studies with its Atridox product for the non-invasive treatment of periodontal disease were successful.
The results were unveiled at the annual meeting here of the International Association for Dental Research, it said.
It said it plans to submit the study data in a New Drug Application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration "early this year."

"The Atridox studies conclusively demonstrate that this therapy, when used by itself, is therapeutically equivalent to scaling and root planing for treating periodontal disease," said Atrix president and chief scientific officer, Lee Southard.

The company said Atridox will provide an additional treatment option that is faster, less painful and less costly than scaling and root planing, which it said is currently used as a standard treatment for periodontitis.

Periodontitis -- inflammation of the supporting structure of the teeth -- is considered to be the second most prevalent disease in the United States after the common cold, and a leading cause of tooth loss, according to Atrix.
Southard said, "Its (atridox's) pending availability to the American public is expected to significantly improve patient compliance with periodontal maintenance therapy."
At present, he said, an estimated 30 to 40 percent of patients who receive scaling and root planing therapy are lost to follow-up maintenance.

Atridox is applied to the infected periodontal pocket as a fluid, where it molds to the shape of the problem area and quickly solidifies, releasing doxycycline for a period of seven days as it is bioabsorbed, Atrix said.
The treatment is intended to be repeated at appropriate intervals as part of a regular periodontal maintenance program, it said.
